patch.objective: Decoupling with queues and pub/sub: Amazon SQS and Amazon SNS

sources.cite: AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Associate (SAA-C03) exam guide (PDF): Design Secure Architectures 30%, Design Resilient Architectures 26%, Design High-Performing Architectures 24%, Design Cost-Optimized Architectures 20%
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch of the PDF on 2026-11-17. Quoted: Task 2.1 'Determining the AWS services required to achieve loose coupling based on requirements', Task 3.2 'Decoupling workloads so that components can scale independently'; Task 1.3 'Encrypting data at rest (for example, AWS KMS)', 'Implementing access policies for encryption keys'; Task 2.2 'Service quotas and throttling', Task 4.4 'Selecting an appropriate throttling strategy'.

sources.cite: AWS Certification, AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Professional certification page (current exam SAP-C03), and Tutorials Dojo, 'What's new with the AWS Certified Solutions Architect Professional SAP-C03'
sources.note: Both read through summarizing fetches on 2026-11-17. The AWS page links the SAP-C03 exam guide and prep plan but shows no domains. The Tutorials Dojo page lists the five SAP-C03 domains (cloud-native architecture design and implementation; security, compliance, and governance; cost-optimized architecture design; resilience, migration, and business continuity; operational excellence and automation) and says SAP-C03 became generally available on November 17, 2026. The weights (25/25/15/15/20) and the objective wording are the course seed's; the official SAP-C03 guide was not read (to verify).

sources.cite: AWS Lambda Developer Guide, Creating and configuring an Amazon SQS event source mapping
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17. Relevant text: by default, after an error 'all messages in that batch return to the queue. After the visibility timeout, the messages become visible to Lambda again'; set the visibility timeout to at least six times the function timeout; Lambda refuses a function timeout longer than the queue's visibility timeout. The case's consumer is a container worker, not Lambda, so this check does not protect it. That a standard queue delivers at least once (so consumers must be idempotent), the 30-second default visibility timeout and ChangeMessageVisibility are from memory of the SQS developer guide (to verify).
